summary.text: 还 is the simplified form of 還. In later forms, 還 is built from 辵, associated with movement, and 瞏, identified as a sound element; its received dictionary gloss is “return.” The visible 不 in 还 does not establish a sound or meaning role in that older construction. Modern 还 also means “still” and “yet,” but the evidence does not establish how these senses relate to “return.”

formation.text: The later 辵/瞏 construction of 還 is phonosemantic: 辵 contributes a movement-related meaning, and 瞏 is identified as the sound element. A separate analysis proposes that 瞏’s “round jade disc” sense also contributes meaning; the received analysis assigns it only a phonetic role. Reported early forms have different component analyses, and the evidence does not establish their transition to this later construction.

components.text: In 还, 辶 is the conventional side form of 辵. 辵 is identified as movement-related in later forms of 還, but that analysis does not apply to every reported early form.

不 is visible in modern 还, whose recorded structure is ⿺辶不. Its appearance does not establish a meaning or sound role in the older 還 construction. A separate dictionary entry records a 不-associated graph 还 but does not connect it to this variant.

In later forms of 還, 瞏 is identified as a sound element. A reported Old Chinese comparison gives *ɡʷraːn for 還 and *ɡʷeŋ for 睘; the evidence does not independently establish 睘’s identity, reading, or phonetic fit here. One analysis also proposes a meaning contribution from its “round jade disc” sense, while the received analysis assigns it only a phonetic role.

sound_limitation.text: The reported Old Chinese comparison does not independently establish that 睘 is the component intended in 還 or verify the proposed phonetic fit.

sound.text: A reported Old Chinese comparison pairs 還 *ɡʷraːn with 睘 *ɡʷeŋ; this is a proposed historical sound relationship, not an independently verified fit.

history.text: Early forms of 還 are described with differing analyses: some oracle-bone forms are analyzed as 行/目/方, while a separate Zhouyuan form is described as 彳/睘. Later bronze and seal forms are analyzed with 辵 and 睘. These source descriptions do not establish a continuous graphic transition; the glyph images were not visually inspected.

The received dictionary analysis writes 還 as 从辵瞏聲. The graph 还 is documented as a graphic variant of 還 and is used as its simplified form. A separate dictionary entry associates a graph 还 with 不 and other readings, but does not establish a connection to this variant.

uncertainties.text: The connection between the reported early forms and the later 辵/瞏 construction is unclear. The separately recorded 不-associated graph 还 is not established as part of the modern variant’s history.

The received analysis identifies 瞏 as the phonetic element, and a reported Old Chinese comparison exists, but the evidence does not independently establish the component’s identity or verify the sound fit.

senses.text: The received dictionary glosses 還 as 復, “return/repeat,” and cited classical material records the sense “return.” Exact dates for the cited works and artifacts are not given here.

senses.period: bronze and classical attestations; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: 還 is attested with the sense “go around” or “circle.” Its chronological relation to “return” is not established.
A classical citation uses 還 to mean “immediately.” Its relation to “return” or other senses is not established.

senses.period: Tang citations and later uses; exact chronology unresolved
senses.text: Adverbial uses include “still” and “yet”; a Tang citation has the sense “still/again.” No dated chain connects these uses to “return.”

senses.period: later cited uses; exact chronology unresolved
senses.text: Cited uses include “also,” “more,” and “besides.” Their individual chronology and any path from “return” are not established.

limitations.text: The cited sources document several senses but do not establish a dated sequence or semantic bridges from “return” to “still,” “yet,” “also,” “more,” or “immediately.”

In cited manuscript passages, 還 is proposed as a sound-based spelling for 懷 and 環: the written sign was reused for other words thought to have sounded alike or similarly. The cited material supplies no pronunciation comparisons to demonstrate either match, so these spellings do not show meanings developing from “return.”

overview.text: 还 is the simplified form of 還, whose attested meaning includes “return; go back.” Later 還 combines a movement-related element with a sound element. Modern 还 also means “still” and “yet,” but the sources do not establish a path from “return” to those senses.

不 appears in modern 还, but is not established as part of the older 還 construction.
The reported comparison proposes a sound relationship for 睘 and 還, though it does not independently verify the component identity or fit.

takeaway.text: The visible 不 in 还 does not establish a sound role in the older 還 construction.

relationships.text: 辶 is the side form of 辵, identified as the movement-related component in later 還; 还 is documented as a graphic variant of 還.

The received analysis identifies 瞏 as the sound component in later forms of 還. A reported Old Chinese comparison is available, but the evidence does not independently verify the component identity or fit.
还 is documented as a graphic variant of 還 and is used as its modern simplified form.
